docs.title: AI Codebase Knowledge Builder
docs.text: Ever stared at a new codebase written by others feeling completely lost? This project analyzes GitHub repositories and creates beginner-friendly tutorials explaining exactly how the code works - all powered by AI! Our intelligent system automatically breaks down complex codebases into digestible explanations that even beginners can understand.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Clone this repository 

    git clone https://github.com/ardennguyen/Codebase-Knowledge-Builder

  2. Install dependencies (we highly recommend using a virtual environment of your choice like venv, conda, uv, or pyenv to avoid polluting your global system): 

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  3. Set up LLM in utils/call_llm.py by providing credentials via a .env file. You can use native Gemini by setting GEMINI_API_KEY. For OpenRouter, set LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER and OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

  4. Generate a complete codebase tutorial by running the main script: 

    # Analyze a GitHub repository
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --include "*.py" "*.js" --exclude "tests/*" --max-size 50000

# Or, analyze a local directory
python main.py --dir /path/to/your/codebase --include "*.py" --exclude "*test*"

# Or, generate a tutorial in Vietnamese
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --language "Vietnamese"

docs.title: CLI Options
docs.text:
• --repo or --dir - Specify either a GitHub repo URL or a local directory path (required, mutually exclusive)
  • -n, --name - Project name (optional, derived from URL/directory if omitted)
  • -t, --token - GitHub token (or set GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable)
  • -o, --output - Output directory (default: ./output)
  • -i, --include - Files to include (e.g., *.py *.js). Defaults to * (all files).
  • -e, --exclude - Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.
  • -s, --max-size - Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200KB)
  • --language - Language for the generated tutorial (default: "english")
  • --max-abstractions - Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10)
  • --no-cache - Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled)
  • --thinking-level - Thinking effort level for native Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama reasoning models (e.g., low, medium, high). Leave empty to use model defaults.
  • --max-tokens - Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically from the model).
  • --mode - Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial)
  • --advanced - Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced
  • --mkdocs - Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet)
  • --incremental - Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference)
  • --force-rebuild - Clear incremental cache and regenerate all chapters from scratch (use with --incremental)
  • --batch - Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).
  • --force-batch - Force the pipeline to use map-reduce mode regardless of context limits.
  • --debug - Enable verbose debug output.
  • --cleanup - Clean up logs and cache JSON at the end of the script (default: No).

The application will crawl the repository, analyze the codebase structure, generate tutorial content in the specified language, and save the output in the specified directory (default: ./output). This includes individual chapter files, an index.md, and a compiled full_content.md containing the complete tutorial with a Table of Contents.

Built using Pocket Flow, a 100-line LLM framework.

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
Notes for AI: Keep it simple and clear. If the requirements are abstract, write concrete user stories

User Story: As a developer onboarding to a new codebase, I want a tutorial automatically generated from its GitHub repository or local directory, optionally in a specific language. The system supports four documentation styles: a tutorial mode that explains core abstractions with beginner-friendly language, analogies, and code walkthroughs; an advanced mode that produces architecture deep-dives aimed at senior developers or PMs joining a project mid-way, covering design patterns, key dependencies, and practical onboarding notes; an api-reference mode that generates exhaustive, formal API documentation for every code module (1:1 file-to-chapter mapping); and an sdk mode that produces SDK-style integration guides. The system must also gracefully handle codebases of any size by dynamically switching to a Map-Reduce approach when context limits are reached.

Input: - A publicly accessible GitHub repository URL or a local directory path. - A project name (optional, will be derived from the URL/directory if not provided). - Desired language for the tutorial (optional, defaults to English). - Advanced configurations: documentation style (--mode), token scaling (--max-tokens, --batch, --force-batch), prompting (--thinking-level, --max-abstractions), caching (--no-cache), output format (--mkdocs, --incremental), debugging (--debug), and execution cleanup (--cleanup).

Output: - A directory named after the project containing: - An index.md file with: - A high-level project summary (potentially translated). - A Mermaid flowchart diagram visualizing relationships between abstractions (using potentially translated names/labels). - An ordered list of links to chapter files (using potentially translated names). - A link to full_content.md at the bottom. - Individual Markdown files for each chapter (01_chapter_one.md, 02_chapter_two.md, etc.) detailing core abstractions in a logical order (potentially translated content). - A full_content.md (inside the project subdirectory) containing all merged chapters and a Table of Contents. - When --mkdocs is used: YAML frontmatter is injected into every chapter, filenames mirror source directory structure instead of numbered prefixes, and a nav_snippet.yml navigation file is generated for MkDocs integration. - When --incremental is used (api-reference mode only): a .doc_cache_manifest.json tracks MD5 hashes of source files to skip regeneration of unchanged modules across runs.

docs.title: 2. Flow Design
docs.text: Notes for AI: 1. Consider the design patterns of agent, map-reduce, rag, and workflow. Apply them if they fit. 2. Present a concise, high-level description of the workflow.

docs.title: Applicable Design Pattern:
docs.text:
This project primarily uses a Workflow pattern with dynamic branching into a Map-Reduce pattern. The chapter writing step also utilizes a BatchNode.

  1. Workflow & Routing: The overall process fetches code, estimates token payloads, and routes based on context limits. If the codebase fits the LLM window, it goes directly to abstraction identification.
  2. Map-Reduce: If the codebase exceeds context limits (or if forced), the codebase is grouped into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (each batch stays under the effective token limit and never mixes files from different directories). A MapAbstractions BatchNode processes each batch individually, and a ReduceAbstractions Node merges them into a global list.
  3. Batch Processing: The WriteChapters node processes each identified abstraction independently (map) before final tutorial compilation.

docs.title: Flow high-level Design:
docs.text:
1. FetchRepo: Crawls the specified repository/directory using crawl_github_files or crawl_local_files.
  2. ContextRouter: Analyzes the total token payload of the fetched files using tiktoken. Dynamically calculates prompt overhead (template tokens + directory tree tokens) and computes an effective limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead. If --mode api-reference is used, routes to "deterministic". If the file content tokens exceed this effective limit or if --force-batch is used, it chunks files into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (never mixing files from different directories) and routes to "batch". Also builds a compact directory tree of all files (stored in shared["directory_tree"]) for cross-batch awareness. With --debug, displays detailed per-batch file lists and token breakdowns. Otherwise, it routes to "direct".
  3. Path A: Direct
    • IdentifyAbstractions: Analyzes the entire codebase at once to identify core abstractions.
  4. Path B: Map-Reduce
    • MapAbstractions (BatchNode): Analyzes each localized directory chunk to extract partial abstractions. Each batch receives the full directory tree for cross-batch awareness.
    • ReduceAbstractions: Merges overlapping/partial abstractions into a global list of architecture components.
  5. Path C: Deterministic (api-reference mode)
    • DeterministicFileMapper: Bypasses LLM-based abstraction discovery entirely. Uses a lightweight LLM call to filter out non-code files (configs, UI layouts, static assets), then creates a 1:1 mapping of each code file to a documentation module. Skips AnalyzeRelationships and OrderChapters, routing directly to WriteChapters.
  6. AnalyzeRelationships (Paths A & B only): Takes the unified abstractions list (from either path) and generates a high-level project summary and relationships diagram. Uses token-budget-aware file inclusion: the budget is split evenly across abstractions, with unused budget redistributed in a second pass, maximizing code context without exceeding the context window.
  7. OrderChapters (Paths A & B only): Determines the most logical sequence to present the abstractions.
  8. WriteChapters (BatchNode): Iterates through the ordered abstractions and writes detailed Markdown chapters using context-aware code inclusion.
  9. CombineTutorial: Assembles the final outputs including index.md, individual chapter files, and a compiled full_content.md.
flowchart TD
    A[FetchRepo] --> Router[ContextRouter]

    Router -->|direct| B[IdentifyAbstractions]
    Router -->|batch| M1[MapAbstractions]
    Router -->|deterministic| DFM[DeterministicFileMapper]
    M1 --> M2[ReduceAbstractions]

    B --> C[AnalyzeRelationships]
    M2 --> C

    C --> D[OrderChapters]
    D --> E[Batch WriteChapters]
    DFM --> E
    E --> F[CombineTutorial]

def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None,
                      max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True) -> dict:
    # Returns: {"files": {relative_path_str: content_str, ...}}

Directory Pruning Algorithm (critical for nested directories like Core.User/.vs/): 

# During os.walk, for each subdirectory d:
excluded_dirs = set()
for d in dirs:
    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), directory)
    # Check .gitignore first
    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
        excluded_dirs.add(d)
        continue
    # Check exclude patterns — strip trailing /* for directory matching
    if exclude_patterns:
        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
            dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                break
# Remove matched dirs to prevent os.walk descent
for d in dirs.copy():
    if d in excluded_dirs:
        dirs.remove(d)

Note: Directory validation: raises ValueError if directory path doesn't exist. Loads .gitignore with utf-8-sig encoding (BOM-safe). All directories and files are sorted() for deterministic traversal order.

Progress Display Format: - Green (\033[92m): [processed] — Successfully read files - Gray (\033[90m): [excluded (.gitignore)] / [excluded (not in include list)] — Skipped by pattern - Red (\033[91m): [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB] — Exceeded max_file_size - Red (\033[91m): [cannot process: not a text file] / [cannot process: {e}] — Binary/encoding errors

Note: After crawling, prints a --- Crawl Summary --- block with total found, processed, excluded, size limited, and non-text counts.

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:

    try:
        repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)

    files = {}
    skipped_files = []

    # --- ANSI colors ---
    C_GREEN  = "\033[92m"
    C_GRAY   = "\033[90m"
    C_RED    = "\033[91m"
    C_RESET  = "\033[0m"

    # --- Counters ---
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_list = []
    skipped_non_text_list = []
    entry_num = 0

    # --- Load .gitignore (BOM-safe) ---
    gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
    gitignore_spec = None
    if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
        try:
            with open(gitignore_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
        except Exception:
            pass

    for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
        # --- Directory pruning (same algorithm as crawl_local_files) ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
            reason = None
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                reason = "excluded (.gitignore)"
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = "excluded"
                        break
            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {dirpath_rel}/ [{reason}]{C_RESET}")

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)
        dirs.sort()  # Deterministic traversal order

        # --- File processing ---
        for filename in sorted(filenames):
            abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
            rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
            entry_num += 1

            if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
            except OSError:
                continue

            if file_size > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                size_kb = file_size / 1024
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                with open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files[rel_path] = content
                count_processed += 1
                print(f"{C_GREEN}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [processed]{C_RESET}")
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: not a text file]{C_RESET}")
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: {e}]{C_RESET}")

    # --- Crawl Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    print(f"\n--- Crawl Summary ---")
    print(f"  Total found : {total_fetched}")
    print(f"{C_GREEN}  Processed   : {count_processed}{C_RESET}")
    if count_excluded > 0:
        print(f"{C_GRAY}  Excluded    : {count_excluded}{C_RESET}")
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Size limit  : {count_size_limit}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_size_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    if count_non_text > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Non-text    : {count_non_text}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_non_text_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    print(f"---------------------")

    return {
        "files": files,
        "stats": {
            "downloaded_count": len(files),
            "skipped_count": len(skipped_files),
            "skipped_files": skipped_files,
            "base_path": None,
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
            "source": "ssh_clone"
        }
    }

Step 4 — Recursive Content Fetching (1 API call per directory): 

def fetch_contents(path):
    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
    params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

    # Rate limit handling with header-based wait:
    if response.status_code in (403, 429) and 'rate limit exceeded' in response.text.lower():
        if not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Provide a token.")
        reset_time = int(response.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Reset', 0))
        wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
        time.sleep(wait_time)
        return fetch_contents(path)  # Recursive retry

    contents = response.json()
    if not isinstance(contents, list):
        contents = [contents]

    for item in contents:
        if item["type"] == "file":
            # Check patterns, size, then fetch content
            # Path A: Use download_url directly, check Content-Length header
            # Path B (fallback): If no download_url, GET item["url"],
            #   base64 decode with size estimate: len(content) * 0.75 > max_file_size
        elif item["type"] == "dir":
            # Check gitignore + exclude before recursing
            fetch_contents(item["path"])

Step 5 — Dual Content Fetch Strategy: 

# Path A: download_url available
if "download_url" in item and item["download_url"]:
    file_response = requests.get(item["download_url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_length = int(file_response.headers.get('content-length', 0))
    if content_length > max_file_size:  # Final size check
        continue
    files[rel_path] = file_response.text

# Path B: base64 fallback
else:
    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_data = content_response.json()
    if len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75 > max_file_size:  # Approximate size
        continue
    file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode('utf-8')
    files[rel_path] = file_content

Provide a token." | | 403/429 | With token | Sleep using X-RateLimit-Reset header, recursive retry |

Notes for AI: Prompt templates are in prompts/tutorial/, prompts/advanced/, prompts/api-reference/, and prompts/sdk/. They contain {placeholder} variables that form a CONTRACT with the node code.

    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)

    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:

def create_token_counter():
    """Create a token counting function using tiktoken with char-count fallback."""
    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The flow.py module defines the structural DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) pipeline for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system using the pocketflow framework. Its primary responsibility is instantiating and wiring together processing nodes imported from nodes, establishing transitions, branch points, retry parameters, and entry points necessary to generate end-to-end technical documentation and tutorials from repository source trees.

The workflow coordinates three distinct architectural analysis pathways based on context routing: 1. Direct Path (direct): Bypasses chunked map-reduce steps for small codebases that fit within standard context windows, directly executing abstraction identification. 2. Batch Path (batch): Employs a map-reduce pipeline (MapAbstractions into ReduceAbstractions) for large repositories requiring chunk-based summarization before relationship analysis. 3. Deterministic Path (deterministic): Uses a direct 1:1 file-to-page mapper (DeterministicFileMapper) designed for exhaustive, file-by-file internal API reference generation, bypassing abstraction synthesis and chapter reordering.

docs.title: create_tutorial_flow()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow() -> Flow:

Description: Constructs and returns the complete PocketFlow execution graph. It instantiates ten pipeline nodes with tailored retry and backoff parameters, establishes deterministic and dynamic transition edges between them, and designates the starting node for pipeline execution.

def create_tutorial_flow():
    fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

The function begins by instantiating nodes defined in nodes. All nodes requiring external LLM synthesis (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, and DeterministicFileMapper) are initialized with max_retries=5 and wait=20 to guarantee resilience against rate limits or transient API connection issues. Structural/local processing nodes (FetchRepo, ContextRouter, and CombineTutorial) do not invoke remote LLM endpoints directly and are instantiated with default retry parameters.

Next, the execution graph is configured using pocketflow operator overloads: - >> (unconditional edge) connects single upstream nodes to downstream targets. - - "action" >> (conditional branch) routes execution from ContextRouter based on runtime context size or target mode. - Multiple convergence points are established: identify_abstractions and reduce_abstractions both feed into analyze_relationships, while order_chapters and deterministic_mapper both feed into write_chapters.

Finally, the function returns an initialized pocketflow.Flow instance whose entry point is bound to fetch_repo.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * Flow: An initialized pocketflow.Flow instance configured with the complete directed graph starting at FetchRepo.

Raises: * No exceptions are explicitly raised by the construction logic itself.

Example: 

# Calling create_tutorial_flow from the main application entry point:
from flow import create_tutorial_flow

flow = create_tutorial_flow()

The main.py module serves as the primary command-line interface (CLI) entry point for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder engine. docs.title: DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS
docs.text:
• Type: set[str]
  • Value: {"*"}
  • Description: Baseline file inclusion pattern matching all files encountered during repository crawling unless filtered out by exclusion rules.

docs.title: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS
docs.text:
• Type: set[str]
  • Description: Exhaustive set of glob patterns automatically ignored during repository traversal across local and remote sources. Categorized into seven distinct domains:
  • Media, Data, and Static Assets: Binary image files (.png, .jpg, .ico, .webp), audio/video files (.mp4, .mp3, .wav), document containers (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx), archives (.zip, .tar, .gz), and raw directories (assets/*, static/*, temp/*).
  • Build, Distribution, and Framework Caches: Compiled frontend/backend output directories (dist/*, build/*, out/*, .next/*, .nuxt/*, .svelte-kit/*), documentation/example directories (docs/*, test/*, tests/*, examples/*), and temporary editor swap files (*.swp, *.bak, *.log).
  • Environments, Dependencies, and Lockfiles: Virtual environments (.venv/*, env/*), environment files (.env*), third-party dependency vendor trees (node_modules/*, vendor/*, packages/*), and package lockfiles (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, Cargo.lock, poetry.lock).
  • Language-Specific Exclusions: Python byte code (__pycache__/*, *.pyc), test coverage artifacts (.pytest_cache/*, .coverage, htmlcov/*), Java/JVM artifacts (*.class, *.jar, *.war), native C/C++ compiled binaries (*.o, *.obj, *.dll, *.dylib, *.so), and mobile build trees (ios/Pods/*, android/.gradle/*).
  • OS & Version Control: VCS control directories (.git/*, .github/*, .svn/*, .hg/*) and OS-specific metadata files (.DS_Store, Thumbs.db, desktop.ini).
  • Classic IDEs: IDE workspace configuration folders (.vscode/*, .idea/*, .eclipse/*, *.iml).
  • AI Agents & Modern AI IDEs: Metadata and rule configurations from AI code assistants and agents (.cursor/*, .cursorrules, .windsurf/*, .windsurfrules, .cline/*, .clinerules, .roo/*, .agent/*, .continue/*, .gemini/*, .claude/*, .copilot/*).

Description: Parses command-line arguments, validates execution parameters, configures LLM runtime options, prepares the global state dictionary, and dispatches the execution graph through create_tutorial_flow.

The function enforces key constraints: * Requires either --repo or --dir via a mutually exclusive argument group. * Validates incremental caching: if --incremental is supplied with a mode other than api-reference, the flag is automatically disabled because non-reference modes lack deterministic 1:1 file-to-chapter mapping. * Processes --force-rebuild when running in incremental mode by locating and removing the .doc_cache_manifest.json file before the pipeline executes. * Identifies the active LLM provider (evaluating LLM_PROVIDER, GEMINI_PROJECT_ID, or GEMINI_API_KEY) and fetches the context window limit dynamically via get_model_context_length from utils.call_llm if --max-tokens is not explicitly provided. * Constructs the shared dictionary containing runtime arguments, inclusion/exclusion rules, and placeholders for downstream pipeline nodes to populate. * Executes the flow and handles teardown of logs and cache files when --cleanup is enabled.

Visibility: Public Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data: list[tuple[str, str]], indices: list[int]) -> dict[str, str]:

Description: Retrieves file path keys and source code contents from a global indexed file list given a list of target integer indices. It constructs a lookup map where the key is formatted as "{index} # {path}" to provide surrounding context to the language model.

Parameters: * files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): Sequence of (path, content) tuples representing all crawled source files. * indices (list[int]): List of integer indices to extract.

Returns: * dict[str, str]: Mapping of formatted file index headers to raw file content strings.

Raises: * None (out-of-bounds indices are ignored via boundary checks).

Example: 

def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content  # Use index + path as key for context
    return content_map

The function iterates over the target index list and verifies that each index falls within 0 <= i < len(files_data). If valid, it extracts the tuple and populates the dictionary with a composite key consisting of the integer index and file path. This helper guarantees safe access to repository content during chapter compilation and abstraction analysis without raising indexing exceptions.

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode

    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        return f.read()

This helper handles path resolution relative to the nodes.py directory location, preventing path mismatches when the CLI is executed from different working directories. It opens the target file using UTF-8 with BOM signature compatibility (utf-8-sig) to ensure cross-platform compatibility across Windows, Linux, and macOS environments.

Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response: str) -> Any:

Description: Extracts and deserializes structured YAML data embedded within triple-backtick ```yaml fenced code blocks from an LLM completion response.

Parameters: * response (str): Raw completion text returned by the model.

Returns: * Any: Parsed Python data structure (typically a dict or list).

def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e

The function performs string splitting against delimiter boundaries ```yaml and ``` to isolate the payload. The extracted substring is passed to yaml.safe_load(). Any deserialization failure or missing code fence error is caught and re-raised as a ValueError with detailed exception context, triggering upstream node retry mechanisms.

def create_token_counter():

    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    except Exception:
        return lambda text: len(text) // 4

The returned closure evaluates arbitrary strings while disabling special token syntax checking (disallowed_special=()), preventing tokenizer exceptions when analyzing raw source files containing syntax that resembles special tokens.     @staticmethod

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> str | list[list[tuple[int, str, str]]]:

Description: Partitions files into directory-isolated batches when the batch route is selected, ensuring individual batches do not cross directory boundaries or exceed token and size limits.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Unpacked parameter tuple from prep().

Returns: * str | list[list[tuple[int, str, str]]]: "direct", "deterministic", or a list of file batches where each batch contains (index, path, content) items.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, directory_tree, debug = prep_res
        llm_logger.info(
            f"NODE EXEC | node=ContextRouter | action=route_decision | route={route} | files={len(files_data)} | effective_limit={effective_limit:,}"
        )

        if route == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if route == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"

        # Group by directory for coherence, with pre-computed tokens
        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

        # Build token-aware batches (never mix directories)
        batches = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
            current_batch = []
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
                # Start new batch if adding this file would exceed effective limit or file count cap
                if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                    batches.append(current_batch)
                    current_batch = []
                    current_tokens = 0

                current_batch.append((i, path, content))
                current_tokens += tokens

            # Flush remaining files in this directory
            if current_batch:
                batches.append(current_batch)

        batch_word = "batch" if len(batches) == 1 else "batches"
        print(f"\033[93m[Capacity] Split into {len(batches)} {batch_word}.\033[0m")
        llm_logger.info(f"NODE COMPLETE | node=ContextRouter | route={route} | batches={len(batches)}")

        // ... [debug logging] ...
        self._directory_tree = directory_tree
        return batches

When batching is required, files are grouped by their directory (os.path.dirname). The method iterates through directories in sorted order and creates new batches whenever adding a file would exceed either effective_limit or batch_size. This ensures batches maintain directory coherence.

            max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
            safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
            count_tokens = create_token_counter()

            context = ""
            file_info = []  # Store tuples of (index, path)
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
                entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
                entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)

                if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                    print(f"\033[93mWarning: Context truncated at file index {i} ({path}) to fit within limit of {safety_limit} tokens.\033[0m")
                    break

                context += entry
                file_info.append((i, path))
                current_tokens += entry_tokens

            return context, file_info  # file_info is list of (index, path)

        context, file_info = create_llm_context(files_data)
        file_listing_for_prompt = "\n".join([f"- {idx} # {path}" for idx, path in file_info])

            file_listing_for_prompt,
            len(files_data),
            project_name,
            language,
            use_cache,
            max_abstraction_num,
            thinking_level,
            shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
            shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
            shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),

Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Allocates file snippet token budgets across abstractions using a two-pass redistribution algorithm to prevent starvation, then prepares the prompt context.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary.

Returns: * tuple: Context string, abstraction listing, abstraction count, project name, language, and configuration flags.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

        // ... [initializes context string and calculates total budget] ...

        # Two-pass allocation:
        # Pass 1: give each abstraction an equal share, track unused
        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions that need more
        per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
        included_indices = set()
        abstr_results = []

        for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
            budget = per_abstr_budget
            included_files = []
            remaining_files = []
            for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
                if idx in included_indices:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                    continue
                if tokens <= budget:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                    budget -= tokens
                    included_indices.add(idx)
                else:
                    remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions with remaining files
        total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
        if total_unused > 0:
            for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
                if not remaining_files or total_unused <= 0:
                    continue
                still_remaining = []
                for idx, path, file_content, tokens in remaining_files:
                    if idx in included_indices:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                        continue
                    if tokens <= total_unused:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                        total_unused -= tokens
                        included_indices.add(idx)
                    else:
                        still_remaining.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                abstr_results[i] = (included_files, still_remaining, 0)

        // ... [builds context output string] ...
        return (
            context,
            "\n".join(abstraction_info_for_prompt),
            num_abstractions,
            project_name,
            language,
            use_cache,
            thinking_level,
            shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
            shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
            shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
        )

The method divides the available snippet token budget equally among abstractions in Pass 1. In Pass 2, any remaining budget is redistributed to abstractions with additional pending files. Files that appear across multiple abstractions are referenced by index rather than duplicated, maximizing context efficiency.

            response = call_llm(
                prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level
            )

            ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)
            if not isinstance(ordered_indices_raw, list):
                raise ValueError("LLM output is not a list")

            ordered_indices = []
            seen_indices = set()
            for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
                if isinstance(entry, int):
                    idx = entry
                elif isinstance(entry, str) and "#" in entry:
                    idx = int(entry.split("#")[0].strip())
                else:
                    idx = int(str(entry).strip())

                if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions):
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid index {idx} in ordered list. Max index is {num_abstractions - 1}.")
                if idx in seen_indices:
                    raise ValueError(f"Duplicate index {idx} found in ordered list.")
                ordered_indices.append(idx)
                seen_indices.add(idx)

            if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Ordered list length ({len(ordered_indices)}) does not match number of abstractions ({num_abstractions}). Missing indices: {set(range(num_abstractions)) - seen_indices}"
                )

            return ordered_indices
        except Exception as e:

        for section in sections:
            lines.append(f"{heading} {section['name']}")
            lines.append("")
            if section.get("modules"):
                lines.append("| Module | Description |")
                lines.append("|--------|-------------|")
                for mod_name in section["modules"]:
                    match = next((cf for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] == mod_name), None)
                    if match:
                        display = mod_name.split(".")[-1] if "." in mod_name else mod_name
                        desc = match["description"]
                        if desc.startswith("Internal API reference"):
                            content_lines = match["content"].strip().split("\n")
                            for cl in content_lines:
                                cs = cl.strip()
                                if cs and not cs.startswith(("---", "#", "```", "title:", "sidebar_position:")):
                                    desc = cs[:120]
                                    break
                        lines.append(f"| [{display}](api/{match['filename']}) | {desc} |")
                lines.append("")
            for child in section.get("children", []):
                CombineTutorial._build_index_sections(lines, [child], chapter_files, level + 1)

The method recursively processes section hierarchies. For each module, it extracts a description from either the module metadata or the first paragraph of the generated chapter content, formatting the entries into a Markdown table.

docs.text:
The utils/__init__.py file serves as the package initialization entry point for the utils namespace within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. In Python's module and package hierarchy, this file establishes the utils directory as a regular Python package, enabling consumers—such as flow, main, and nodes—to import utility submodules directly via absolute or relative dot notation.

By maintaining an empty initialization file, the project enforces explicit, granular module imports (e.g., from utils.token_utils import ... or from utils.call_llm import ...) rather than populating a bloated top-level namespace at package load time. This design minimizes circular import hazards, avoids unintended side effects during initial module parsing, and defers the loading of heavier dependencies (such as language model API wrappers or tree-sitter parsers) until their respective utility submodules are explicitly referenced.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils.call_llm module provides an abstraction layer for interacting with Large Language Model (LLM) backends within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It manages model execution routing, caching, run-level logging, and token budgeting parameters across multiple provider endpoints, including Google Gemini (via Vertex AI or Gemini Developer API), OpenRouter, and Ollama (or any standard OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions server).

The module enforces standard structured generation flows by providing: 1. Dynamic Provider Resolution: Automatically inspects environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER, GEMINI_PROJECT_ID, GEMINI_API_KEY) to select between direct Google Gemini SDK calls and OpenAI-compatible HTTP requests. 2. Local Response Caching: Implements a simple disk-backed JSON cache (llm_cache.json) to prevent redundant LLM invocations during development and multi-stage workflow testing. 3. Reasoning/Thinking Budget Adaptation: Translates standardized string levels (low, medium, high) into provider-specific reasoning configurations (such as types.ThinkingConfig for Gemini or payload parameters like reasoning / think / reasoning_effort for OpenRouter and Ollama). 4. Context Length Discovery: Queries provider endpoints (such as OpenRouter's model catalog) or applies heuristic defaults to retrieve maximum context windows for prompt fitting. 5. Session-Specific File Logging: Configures decoupled file-based logging isolated from root loggers, storing complete prompts, execution timing, token statistics, and raw responses.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name: str = "project", mode: str = "tutorial") -> str:

Description: Configures run-specific file-based logging for the execution session. It creates the target log directory (controlled by LOG_DIR, default "logs"), sanitizes project_name and mode to guarantee filesystem safety, clears existing handlers (including NullHandler), and attaches a logging.FileHandler using UTF-8 encoding. It logs an initial banner with execution metadata and returns the resolved log file path.

Parameters: * project_name (str): Name of the repository or project being processed. Defaults to "project". * mode (str): Operational mode of the pipeline (e.g., "tutorial", "documentation"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: Absolute or relative path to the generated log file.

Raises: * OSError: If directory creation or file initialization fails due to insufficient permissions or invalid paths.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/call_llm.py configure_logging implementation
log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

# Sanitize project name for filesystem safety
safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
log_file = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

# Remove any existing handlers (e.g., NullHandler) and add the file handler
logger.handlers.clear()
file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
file_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"))
logger.addHandler(file_handler)

The function ensures that each execution session creates an isolated log file formatted as {safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{YYYYMMDD_HHmmss}.log. By clearing existing handlers before adding the new file handler, it transitions the module from its initial silent NullHandler state to active file recording without duplicate logs. The header block printed at the top of the log captures the startup parameters, ensuring traceability across multi-stage runs.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Queries the OpenRouter catalog endpoint (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models) to retrieve metadata for a given model ID. It caches the API response in the module-level global variable _openrouter_models_cache upon the first request to eliminate redundant HTTP overhead on subsequent lookups.

Parameters: * model_id (str): The model identifier string to match (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet").

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum context window token limit for a given endpoint and model name. If the endpoint corresponds to Google Gemini (generativelanguage.googleapis.com or gemini in model name), it returns 1,000,000. If the endpoint belongs to OpenRouter, it queries OpenRouter's model endpoint and extracts context_length. For unhandled endpoints or upon network failure, it defaults to 100,000.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): Base URL or endpoint of the LLM server. * model_name (str): Target model name. * api_key (str, optional): API key for authenticated requests. Defaults to "".

Returns: * int: The resolved context length limit in tokens.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/call_llm.py get_model_context_length implementation
default_limit = 100000
try:
    if not endpoint_url:
        return default_limit

    if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
        # Safely default to 1M tokens for Gemini models
        return 1000000

    if "openrouter.ai" in endpoint_url:
        resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
        data = resp.json().get("data", [])
        for m in data:
            if m.get("id") == model_name:
                return m.get("context_length", default_limit)
except Exception as e:
    logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch context length for {model_name} at {endpoint_url}: {e}")

return default_limit

This helper is used when planning context window consumption and token allocations across document crawling and prompt generation stages. It incorporates defensive parsing around remote network calls to ensure that downstream prompt construction does not fail if metadata discovery is unreachable.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches an HTTP POST request to an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint for providers configured via environment variables (such as OPENROUTER or OLLAMA). Reads {provider}_MODEL, {provider}_BASE_URL, and optionally {provider}_API_KEY. It constructs the JSON payload, applies reasoning/thinking configurations when requested, executes the HTTP request with timeout limits (10, 300), validates JSON integrity and response structures, and extracts the generated content.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The raw text prompt to send to the model. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The completion string extracted from choices[0].message.content.

Raises: * ValueError: If LLM_PROVIDER, model, or base URL environment variables are missing; if the provider returns invalid JSON; or if the response lacks the choices key. * Exception: Wraps underlying requests.exceptions.HTTPError, requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout, or general requests.exceptions.RequestException instances with descriptive error messages.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/call_llm.py _call_llm_provider implementation
# ...
payload = {
    "model": model,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    "temperature": 0.7,
}

if provider == "OPENROUTER" and thinking_level:
    model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
    if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
        supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])
        if thinking_level.lower() in supported_efforts:
            payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()}
            payload["temperature"] = 1.0  # Required for many reasoning models
        else:
            logger.warning(f"Invalid thinking level '{thinking_level}' for model {model}. Supported efforts: {supported_efforts}")
    else:
        logger.warning(f"Model {model} does not support reasoning via OpenRouter API.")

elif provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
    # Some Ollama SDKs / API versions look for `think`, others look for standard `reasoning_effort`
    payload["think"] = thinking_level.lower()
    payload["reasoning_effort"] = thinking_level.lower()
    payload["temperature"] = 1.0

try:
    response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
    # ...
    response_json = response.json()
    response.raise_for_status()

    # Defensive check: API may return 200 with error/rate-limit payload missing 'choices'
    if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
        error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
        logger.warning(f"API returned 200 but no 'choices' in response: {error_detail}")
        raise ValueError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

    return response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
    # ...

The function adapts payload structures depending on the backend. When interfacing with OpenRouter, it verifies that the specified thinking_level is listed within the model's supported_efforts before modifying the payload and forcing temperature: 1.0. It uses a connect/read timeout pair (10, 300) to handle extended inference times on long completions.

docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches generation requests to Google Gemini using the google.genai SDK. It initializes a genai.Client using Vertex AI if GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is present (with optional GEMINI_LOCATION, defaulting to "us-central1"), or via direct API key authentication if GEMINI_API_KEY is provided. If thinking_level is set, it maps "low", "medium", and "high" string values to explicit token budgets (1024, 4096, 8192) via types.ThinkingConfig. Finally, it executes client.models.generate_content and concatenates all text parts from the response candidates, filtering out non-text metadata.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The prompt text to process. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning level string ("low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The concatenated text content from candidate response parts, or an empty string if no candidates exist.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is defined in the execution environment.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/call_llm.py _call_llm_gemini implementation
if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
    client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION", "us-central1"))
elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
    client = genai.Client(api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"))
else:
    raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")

kwargs = {"model": model, "contents": [prompt]}

if thinking_level:
    # Map string levels to budgets for the installed SDK version
    budget_map = {"low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192}
    budget = budget_map.get(thinking_level.lower(), 4096)
    thinking_config = types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget)
    kwargs["config"] = types.GenerateContentConfig(thinking_config=thinking_config)

response = client.models.generate_content(**kwargs)

# Extract only text parts to avoid "non-text parts: ['thought_signature']" warnings
if response.candidates and response.candidates[0].content.parts:
    text_parts = [part.text for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts if part.text is not None]
    return "".join(text_parts)
return ""

This method interacts directly with the Google GenAI Python SDK. When reasoning is enabled, Gemini responses can include structured thought chunks and metadata signatures (such as thought_signature). The response parsing logic explicitly loops over response.candidates[0].content.parts and ignores non-text chunks, preventing formatting artifacts or warning messages from contaminating generated markdown output.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary entry point for executing model prompts across the entire repository. It calculates prompt token counts via utils.token_utils.count_tokens, checks the local disk cache if use_cache=True, records detailed execution logs, routes the request to either _call_llm_gemini or _call_llm_provider, measures response latency, updates the disk cache upon completion, and returns the response string.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The full prompt text to be submitted to the model. * use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to inspect and update llm_cache.json. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning intensity ("low", "medium", "high", or None). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The model-generated output text.

Raises: * ValueError: Propagated from underlying provider methods if environment variables are missing or provider responses are malformed. * Exception: Propagated from network failures, HTTP errors, or timeout exceptions.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/call_llm.py call_llm implementation
import time
from utils.token_utils import count_tokens

provider = get_llm_provider()
model = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "unknown"))
prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)

logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
logger.info(
    f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}"
)
logger.info(f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}")

# Check cache if enabled
if use_cache:
    cache = load_cache()
    if prompt in cache:
        cached_response = cache[prompt]
        logger.info(f"CACHE HIT | response_chars={len(cached_response):,}")
        logger.info(f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}")
        logger.info("LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit")
        return cached_response

# Make the actual LLM call
start_time = time.time()
logger.info(f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...")

if provider == "GEMINI":
    response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
    response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

elapsed = time.time() - start_time
logger.info(f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}")
logger.info(f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}")

# Update cache if enabled
if use_cache:
    cache = load_cache()
    cache[prompt] = response_text
    save_cache(cache)
    logger.info("CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache")

logger.info(f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s")
return response_text

docs.text:
Original File Path: utils/crawl_github_files.py

Technical overview and reference documentation for the remote repository crawling module. This utility provides functionality to traverse, filter, and extract file contents from GitHub repositories via the GitHub REST API or via SSH git clones into temporary directories.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils.crawl_github_files module is designed to ingest source code and documentation from GitHub repositories into an in-memory dictionary mapping file paths to their raw string contents. It supports two primary modes of operation depending on the input URL format:

  1. SSH Git Cloning (git@... or .git URLs): Clones the full repository to an OS-managed temporary directory via git.Repo.clone_from, parses local .gitignore files via pathspec, walks the file system tree, filters files by pattern and size, and reads matching UTF-8 text contents into memory.
  2. GitHub REST API Traversal (HTTPS URLs): Parses the URL components (owner, repository name, branch or tree SHA, and subdirectory path), inspects branches and tree objects through https://api.github.com, fetches the remote .gitignore file, and recursively crawls directory contents via contents/{path} endpoints. It includes automatic handling of HTTP rate limiting (403/429) with dynamic sleep backoffs calculated from X-RateLimit-Reset headers.

Both pipelines perform path filtering via fnmatch, .gitignore pattern resolution via pathspec.PathSpec, binary/non-text file exclusion with fallback decoders, and maximum file size thresholds.

Description: Serves as the main entry point for downloading text files from a remote GitHub repository. If an SSH URL (git@ or .git) is provided, the function delegates execution to a local clone workflow inside a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(). If an HTTPS GitHub URL is provided, it parses URL parts, validates branches/trees via the GitHub REST API, fetches .gitignore rules, and recursively navigates directory trees using fetch_contents().

docs.title: should_include_file()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (nested closure inside crawl_github_files) Signature: def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether an individual file meets the inclusion criteria based on the active include_patterns, exclude_patterns, and an optional pathspec.PathSpec gitignore specification.

Parameters: * file_path (str): Full or relative repository path of the target file. * file_name (str): Base filename (e.g., main.py). * gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec | None, optional): Compiled gitignore pattern matcher.

Returns: * bool: True if the file matches inclusion criteria and does not match gitignore or exclusion rules; otherwise False.

Core Implementation: 

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

should_include_file prioritizes positive pattern matching on the file's basename before evaluating negative exclusions against its full path. If include_patterns is set, fnmatch.fnmatch tests file_name. If valid, it verifies that gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path) returns False. Finally, it iterates through exclude_patterns to ensure no negative patterns match file_path.

Description: Invokes the GitHub REST API endpoint GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches to list branch objects for the target repository. Used to determine whether URL path components correspond to multi-segment branch names.

Parameters: * owner (str): GitHub organization or user account name. * repo (str): GitHub repository name.

Returns: * list[dict] | list: A list of branch descriptor dictionaries returned by GitHub, or an empty list upon failure or 404 response.

Raises: * Exception: If HTTP status code 403 or 429 is received and no token is set in headers.

Core Implementation: 

    def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
        """Get brancshes of the repository"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                print(
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable."
                )
            else:
                print(
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    "Please verify the repository exists and the token has access to this repository."
                )
            return []

        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"Error fetching the branches of {owner}/{repo}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return []

        return response.json()

The function executes a synchronous requests.get call with 30-second connect and read timeouts. If access fails with a 404, it prints contextual error messages distinguishing between unauthenticated requests to private repos and insufficient token permissions. Non-200 responses return an empty list.

Description: Recursively crawls files and subdirectories at a given repository path using the GitHub Contents API (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}). Handles pagination/lists, inspects file metadata, filters against exclude patterns and .gitignore, performs file downloads via download_url or base64 decoding, and manages rate-limiting backoffs.

Parameters: * path (str): Repository-relative path to inspect.

Returns: * None: Populates the outer files dictionary and api_counters dictionaries in-place.

Raises: * Exception: When unauthenticated API requests hit rate limits.

    def fetch_contents(path):
        """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
        params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
            if not token:
                raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
            reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
            wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
            print(f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            return fetch_contents(path)

        if response.status_code == 404:
            # ... handles 404 logging ...
            return None

        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"Error fetching {path}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return None

        contents = response.json()
        if not isinstance(contents, list):
            contents = [contents]

        for item in contents:
            item_path = item["path"]
            # ... checks path, directory exclusions, file size limits, and downloads content ...

fetch_contents traverses remote directory trees by evaluating each element returned by the contents API. If an item has type == "dir", it checks directory patterns against .gitignore and exclude_patterns (accounting for trailing /* definitions) before calling fetch_contents(item_path).

For items where type == "file", it checks pattern compliance via should_include_file and verifies item["size"] <= max_file_size. It prefers fetching raw text through item["download_url"]. If download_url is unavailable, it queries item["url"] and decodes base64-encoded file payloads, recording non-text or binary decoding failures into api_counters["non_text"].

def crawl_local_files(
    directory,
    include_patterns=None,
    exclude_patterns=None,
    max_file_size=None,
    use_relative_paths=True,
):

Description: Traverses the specified local directory tree, applies path-matching rules and size thresholds, reads all eligible text files, and returns a dictionary mapping file paths to their string contents. Under the hood, it parses any top-level .gitignore file using pathspec.PathSpec, traverses the tree using os.walk, mutates directory lists in-place to prevent descending into ignored directories, filters file paths against glob patterns with fnmatch.fnmatch, reads files using utf-8-sig encoding, and outputs colored real-time traversal telemetry to stdout.

Parameters: * directory (str): The file system path to the target local directory to be crawled. * include_patterns (set, optional): Set of glob patterns representing files to include (e.g., {"*.py", "*.js"}). If provided, files not matching any pattern are excluded. Defaults to None. * exclude_patterns (set, optional): Set of glob patterns representing files or directory names to exclude (e.g., {"tests/*", "__pycache__/*"}). Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int, optional): Maximum allowable file size in bytes. Files exceeding this limit are skipped. Defaults to None. * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): Flag indicating whether the returned keys and console logs should use paths relative to directory (True) or full paths (False). Defaults to True.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing a single key "files", mapped to an inner dictionary {filepath: content}, where filepath is the relative (or absolute) path and content is the decoded string content.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the provided directory parameter does not exist or is not a valid directory according to os.path.isdir(directory).

docs.text:

    files_dict = {}

    # --- Counters ---
    entry_num = 0
    count_processed = 0

    count_non_text = 0

    # --- Load .gitignore ---
    gitignore_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")

            with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:

The function validates that the target path is a directory. It initializes ANSI color escapes for terminal logging along with counters for processed files, excluded paths, size limit violations, and non-text failures. If a .gitignore file is detected directly in the root of the target directory, it is read with utf-8-sig encoding, and parsed via pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines using the gitwildmatch pattern grammar. If parsing fails, a warning is printed to stdout and traversal proceeds without Git ignore filtering.

docs.title: 2. Subtree Pruning and Directory Filtering
docs.text:
# --- Single-pass: walk, filter, and process inline ---
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
        # --- Directory filtering ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), directory)

            reason = None
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                reason = "excluded (.gitignore)"
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = "excluded"
                        break

            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {dirpath_rel}/ [{reason}]{C_RESET}")

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)

        # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
        dirs.sort()
        # ...

Directory filtering is performed during traversal using os.walk. For each sub-directory in the current root, the crawler evaluates its relative path against gitignore_spec.match_file() and each pattern in exclude_patterns (stripping trailing /* suffixes via pattern.removesuffix("/*")). Any directory matching exclusion criteria is collected into excluded_dirs and pruned in-place from dirs using dirs.remove(d). This pruning ensures os.walk never descends into ignored directory subtrees (e.g., .git, node_modules, .venv), significantly optimizing crawl speed.

docs.title: 3. File Filtering, Size Thresholding, and Ingestion
docs.text:
# --- File processing (inline, sorted) ---
        for filename in sorted(files):
            filepath = os.path.join(root, filename)
            relpath = os.path.relpath(filepath, directory) if use_relative_paths else filepath
            entry_num += 1

            # Check gitignore
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(relpath):
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [excluded (.gitignore)]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            # Check exclude patterns
            excluded = False
            if exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        excluded = True
                        break
            if excluded:
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            # Check include patterns
            if include_patterns:
                matched = False
                for pattern in include_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        matched = True
                        break
                if not matched:
                    count_excluded += 1
                    print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [excluded (not in include list)]{C_RESET}")
                    continue

            # Check size limit
            if max_file_size and os.path.getsize(filepath) > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_limit.append(relpath)
                size_kb = os.path.getsize(filepath) / 1024
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            # Try to read as text
            try:
                with open(filepath, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files_dict[relpath] = content
                count_processed += 1
                print(f"{C_GREEN}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [processed]{C_RESET}")
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [cannot process: not a text file]{C_RESET}")
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [cannot process: {e}]{C_RESET}")

Files within non-excluded directories are evaluated in alphabetical order. Each candidate file path is checked sequentially: first against .gitignore, then against exclude_patterns, then against include_patterns, and finally against max_file_size. If the file passes all checks, the crawler opens and reads it using utf-8-sig encoding to handle UTF-8 text files and automatically strip Byte Order Marks (BOM). If reading fails due to a UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, or other I/O exception, the file is classified as non-text, recorded in skipped_non_text, and omitted from the returned dictionary.

The utils.prompts module provides programmatic prompt constructors, configuration generators, and recursive navigation layout transformers used across the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder execution pipeline. Unlike user-configurable or domain-specific prompt templates located in mode directories (prompts/{mode}/), the utilities in this module generate inline prompts and structural outputs required for deterministic internal nodes.

Visibility: Public Signature: def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:

Description: Constructs an inline LLM prompt for the DeterministicFileMapper node during API reference generation. The prompt instructs the model to inspect an indexed list of all candidate project files and identify only the files containing actual program logic (functions, classes, business logic, endpoints) while filtering out configuration, UI layouts, assets, and project files. The output constraint enforces a strict YAML integer list format containing the indices of valid files.

Parameters: * project_name (str): The name of the codebase or target repository being processed. * file_listing (str): Pre-formatted newline-separated string containing indexed file paths (e.g., 0: src/main.py 1: config.json).

Returns: * str: The complete system/user prompt ready for dispatch to an LLM.

Raises: * No explicit exceptions are raised by this function.

Example: 

def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:
    return (
        f"For the project `{project_name}`, here is the list of all files in the codebase:

"
        f"{file_listing}

"
        f"Your task is to identify WHICH of these files are ACTUAL CODE files that contain "
        f"APIs, functions, classes, or core business logic.
"
        f"EXCLUDE: UI layouts (like .xaml, .storyboard, .html), configuration files "
        f"(like .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini), static assets, build scripts "
        f"(like .csproj, .sln), and documentation.

"
        f"Return ONLY a YAML list of the file indices that should be documented as code modules.

"
        f"```yaml
- 0
- 1
- 3
```"
    )

The returned string directly constrains the LLM output format by providing a concrete few-shot YAML sample block (- 0 - 1 - 3). This formatting constraint allows caller nodes in nodes to deterministically parse the raw LLM response using standard YAML decoders without requiring complex natural language extraction. If non-code files are included in the codebase, the prompt's exclusion rules prevent extraneous files from bloating the downstream chapter generation stages.
